proposed.text: Table VIII.1 of PD 1096 shows that adding a firewall to a Basic R-2 project increases the maximum PSO from 55% to 60%. What is the corresponding effect on the minimum USA?

options.text: Minimum USA decreases from 15% to 10% — more building coverage means less required unpaved area
Minimum USA remains at 15% — the firewall only affects PSO, not the unpaved area requirement
Minimum USA increases from 15% to 20% — greater coverage requires more compensatory open space
Minimum USA is eliminated entirely — firewall structures have no open space requirement under Table VIII.1

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: Table VIII.1 for Basic R-2: without firewall — PSO=55%, ISA=30%, USA=15%, TOSL=45%, MACA=85%. With firewall — PSO=60%, ISA=30%, USA=10%, TOSL=40%, MACA=90%. Adding a firewall increases PSO by 5% (55%→60%) and decreases minimum USA by 5% (15%→10%). The TOSL also drops from 45% to 40%. Option B is incorrect — the firewall does reduce USA. Options C and D are incorrect per Table VIII.1.
proposed.explanation: Firewall allowance: greater PSO justified because shared boundary with fire separation reduces the need for open-space buffers on that side. Basic R-2 without firewall: PSO=55%, USA=15%. Basic R-2 with firewall: PSO=60%, USA=10%. The arithmetic identity still holds: PSO+TOSL=100%; TOSL=ISA+USA.
